items.label: A
items.critique: Dry jailer humour and a flat, repetitive escalation ('Last warning') that reads like a minor Westwood NPC. Plain, a bit lazy, very Nox.

items.label: B
items.critique: The list of petty city rules, the 'Oh, I forgot to mention' afterthought and the jab at wizardry are Westwood's deadpan town humour. The 'later' line is unrelated to the first two, which is typical of the original.

items.label: C
items.critique: Lore-flavour barks with no instruction and a dropped article ('can be dangerous place') read like original, lightly edited text. Stiff, but not built to a template.

items.label: D
items.critique: Problem, villain, 'See X in Y', then a solved-state line: a clean state machine with an exclamation on nearly every sentence. 'Pass, friend -- and watch the road!' is neat, but the structure is too regular.

items.label: E
items.critique: Ceremonious 'great [Class] dispatched to aid our beloved' and 'Delay no longer!' match the campaign's slightly overwrought heralding. The third line is a loose travel warning, as in the original.

items.label: F
items.critique: Same three beats as D/H/I/J, with the Reeve's order and a celebratory 'Bread for everyone!' payoff. Clipped exclamatory sentences, with a 'Not one grain!' second line in the house pattern.

items.label: G
items.critique: Urgent, slightly formal ('Your valor knows no peer') with a page break and repeated directions to the Foreman. Longer sentences and an inconsistent capital in 'foreman' feel authentic.

items.label: H
items.critique: Shut-door, culprit, go-see-NPC, then a reopened-and-celebrate pattern. Every sentence ends in '!' and the follow-up is a two-word 'Locked!' echo.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'No ferry today! Or tomorrow, likely.' has a nice comic beat, but the Reeve, the far bank and the reopened-state cheer follow the same mould as its siblings.

items.label: J
items.critique: The template again (the Reeve, a villain's spies, get X to vouch, then '[Person]'s dead... Go on in!'). The short rhyming 'No word, no way in!' feels written to a style guide.

tells: New texts share one three-state skeleton (blocked by an order, a terse echo, reopened after the quest) that tracks quest state. Westwood's guard lines are looser, often unrelated to each other, and sometimes pure flavour or lore.
Exclamation marks on almost every sentence, in uniformly short sentences. Westwood mixes in periods, longer clauses and the odd stiff formality ('Your valor knows no peer').
Recurring invented office and vocabulary ('the Reeve', 'stranger', 'friend', 'north road') repeated across texts reads like one writer and one map.
Westwood's guards carry deadpan bureaucratic humour (rules lists, afterthoughts, prisoner warnings). The new ones are cheerful and functional, with the joke saved for the final quip.
